caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2145 of 2009
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
Respondents ------ Not represented
parties:
Md. Farid Ahmed Bhuiyan ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Mizanur Rahman Bhuiyan and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in brief, are that plaintiff Nos. 1-4 instituted Title Suit No. 63 of 2002 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Gopalgonj for declaration of their title in respect of the suit land described in the schedule to the plaint and for further declaration that the deed of sale dated 06.08.1985 as allegedly executed by Sayed Ali Fakir and Lokman @ Rokman Mollah in favour of defendant No.  1 is illegal, void, forged and not binding upon the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs' case, in short, is that the land covering an area of 1.70 acres originally belonged to Sayed Ali Fakir and Lokman Mollah @ Rokman Mollah in equal share and accordingly, S.A. record was prepared in their names. While possessing the suit land Sayed Ali Fakir died leaving behind his three sons, namely, Habibar, A. Satter, Majibar and four daughters namely, Futi Begum, Huri Begum, Hena Begum and Jobeda Begum. Habibar died leaving behind three sons, namely, Mafizur, Kamruzzaman and Lalon and three daughters, namely, Helena, Lima, Lina and widow Pari Begum. Abdus Sattar died leaving behind three sons, namely, Masud, Mamun, Milon (Minor) and two daughters, Bina Begum, Kona Begum and wife Jobeda. The heirs of Abdus Satter and Habibar sold .21 acre of land to plaintiff No. 1 by a deed of sale dated 24.02.2000. Lokman Mollah died leaving behind his widow, Amiran Nessa and five sons, namely, Mijraj, Nizam, Faruque, Kalam, Shajahan and three daughters, Abiran Nessa, Rubi Begum and Chaina Begum as his heirs. The heirs of Lokman Mollah sold .40 acre of land to plaintiff Nos. 1-3 by a deed of sale dated 14.12.1999. Futi Begum, Huri Begum and Hena Begum sold .25½ acre of land to plaintiff Nos.1-4 by another deed of sale dated 23.02.2000. The heirs of late Habibar, Quamrul, Mafizur, Helena Begum, Lina Begum and Bina Begum sold .12½ acre of land to plaintiff No. 1 by another deed of sale dated 21.03.2000. In this way, the plaintiffs acquired title to .99 acre out of 1.70 acres of land and have been in possession thereof. Sayed Ali Fakir died on 28.11.1978 and Lokman Mollah died on 04.02.1968 but defendant No. 1 by false personation created the alleged deed of sale No. 1403 dated 06.08.1985 from the Office of the Sub-Registrar at Bagharpara including .03 acre of land of Plot No. 113 of Khatian No. 95 of 34 of Mathurapur Mouza in the schedule to the said deed, which was a fictitious land. The executants of the impugned deed had no title to and possession in that .03 acre of land. In Khatian No. 95 of Mouza-Mathurapur, there was no existence of plot No. 113. Although Lokman alias Rokman Mollah was an illiterate person, someone put his signature in the disputed deed claiming himself to be Lokman Mollah. Some of the heirs of Sayed Ali Fakir and Lokman Mollah created a deed declaring that the said deed was genuine one and the declaration was also fraudulent and void. Defendant No. 1 denied the plaintiff's title to the suit land on 20.10.2001 on the basis of said forged deed; consequently the muse of action of the suit arose. 

 3. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that the instant suit was not maintainable. It is barred by limitation and also barred by principles of waiver, estoppel and acquiescence. His case is that the suit land covering 1.70 acres of S.A. Khatian No. 1184 and .03 acre of Plot No. 113 and S. A. Khatian No. 258 of 34 Mathurapur Moms under P.S. Bagharpara originally belonged to Sayed Ali Fakir and Lokman alias Rokman Mollah. They declared to sell the said 1.73 acres of land and defendant No. 1 decided to purchase the same. Accordingly, they executed and registered the disputed deed in the Office of Bagharpara Sub-Registrar and delivered possession thereof to defendant No.  1. In the said deed of sale, the deed writer erroneously mentioned S. A. Khatian No. 95 instead of S. A. Khatian No. 258 in respect of the land of Mathurapur Mouza. Defendant No. 1 after getting the said deed, mutated his name in the khatian and paid rent to the Government. The plaintiffs uncle Abu Taleb Bhuiyan filed a petition of complaint in the Court of Upazila Magistrate under sections 467 and 120 of the Penal Code from which defendant No. 1 was released by the Court of the Additional District Magistrate on 12.05.1991. Plaintiff No. 1 Mizanur Rahman Bhuiyan was a Naik of Bangladesh Army. At the time of performing his duty at the President's Secretariat, he filed an application before the Bureau of Anti-Corruption bringing similar allegation of forgery and after holding inquiry the Anti-Corruption authority found the allegation to be false. At time of recent revisional survey, the draft khatian was prepared in the name of defendant No. 1 against which, the plaintiffs brought an objection which was ultimately dismissed. Majibar Rahman son of Sayed Ali Fakir and Siraj Mollah, Faraque Mollah and Nijam Mollah sons of Lokman Mollah executed deed No. 5500 dated 25.11.1999 declaring the impugned deed genuine. They have stated that on the basis of the impugned deed dated 06.08.1985; defendant No.  1 had taken delivery of possession of the suit land. The other heirs of Sayed Ali Fakir and Lokman Mollah in collusion with the plaintiffs created some fictitious deeds and after that, the plaintiffs have brought the instant case. The plaintiffs have/had no right, title and interest in the suit land and as such, the suit should be dismissed. 

 9. We have considered the submissions Courtly the learned Advocate, the impugned judge went and the materials on record. Having considered oral and documentary evidence, the trial Count came to a finding that Sayed Ali Fakir died on 28.11.1978 and Lokman Mollah on 04.02.1968, that is, they died before execution of the disputed deed of sale dated 06.08.1985. Considering the evidence on record, the appellate Court also concurred with the aforesaid finding of the trial Court. The High Court Division having taken into consideration the above findings of the Courts below came to a finding that the findings of the Courts below were based on evidence on record and as such those findings of facts were immune from any interference by the revisional Court. The High Court Division noticed that in the disputed deed of sale dated 06.08.1985, 1.03 acre of land of Plot No. 113 of Khatian No. 95 of Mouza-Mathurapur, Police Station-Bagharpara, District-Jessore had been included. The High Court Division P found that defendant No. 1 included the aforesaid .03 acre of land in the schedule to the disputed deed of sale for attracting jurisdiction of the Office of Sub-Registrar of Bagharpara to register that deed. The High Court Division came to a finding that the disputed deed of sale dated 1 06.08.1985 containing non existent and fictitious property only to give jurisdiction to the Office of the Sub-Registrar of Bagharpara, Jessore, was void. In support of the aforesaid finding, the High Court Division rightly relied upon the cases of 9 Syed Kawsar Ali vs. Gahar Kazi and others (1985) 37 DLR (AD) 177 and Md. Nurul Islam vs. Moniruddin Sheikh and others (2005) 10 MLR (AD) 200.
